title: The young bagshy
goal: Recognize nouns in -(Y)ş and -(Y)w, and read a short story about learning the dutar.

intro.text: `-(Y)ş` turns a verb into a noun: *girmek* → *giriş* (entrance), *çykmak* → *çykyş* (exit; performance), *gülmek* → *gülüş* (laugh). After a vowel it is *-ýyş* or *-ýiş*: *ýaşaýyş* (life). A few nouns end in *-uw*: *okuw* (studies), *ýazuw* (writing).

vocab.en: exit; performance, talk (çykyş etmek: to perform, to give a talk)
bagshy (a singer of songs and epics who plays the dutar)
master, teacher (of an art or a craft)

exercises.explain: *gir-* ends in a consonant and has a front vowel: *-iş*.
*ýaşa-* ends in a vowel, so the suffix starts with ý: *-ýyş*.

exercises.question: You're in a museum and want to leave. Which sign do you look for?

exercises.prompt: I finished my studies last year.

exercises.question: **Merdan went to the library to read.** Which is right?

why.1: *Okamagy* is the accusative. For a purpose: *okamaga*.

exercises.explain: *Kitaphana* here is the dative (to the library): the ending fuses with the final a. The purpose is *okamaga*.

exercises.prompt: I want to learn to play the dutar.

exercises.title: Ýaş bagşy
exercises.passage:
Myrat on alty ýaşynda. Ol çagalykdan aýdym aýtmagy gowy görýär. Geçen ýyl ol dutar çalmagy öwrenmek isledi. Kakasy oňa Mary şäherindäki bir bagşy bilen okamagy maslahat berdi. Indi Myrat her şenbe halypasynyň öýüne sapak almaga barýar.

Ilki dutar çalmak kyn boldy. Myradyň barmaklary agyrýardy. Ýöne ol taşlamady: her gün iki sagat çalmaga synanyşdy. Halypasy onuň çalyşyny gowy görýär. Geçen hepde Myrat obadaky toýda ilkinji gezek çykyş etdi. Myhmanlar oňa el çarpdylar. Indi onuň arzuwy uly bagşy bolmak.

glossary.en: to clap (for someone: with the dative)

exercises.translation: Myrat is sixteen. Since he was a child he has loved singing. Last year he wanted to learn to play the dutar. His father advised him to study with a bagshy in the city of Mary. Now every Saturday Myrat goes to his master's house for a lesson. At first, playing the dutar was hard. Myrat's fingers used to hurt. But he didn't give up: every day he tried to play for two hours. His master likes the way he plays. Last week Myrat performed for the first time, at a wedding in the village. The guests applauded him. Now his dream is to become a great bagshy.

questions.q: Why did Myrat start going to a master?
options: He wanted to learn to play the dutar.
He wanted to sing at a wedding.
questions.explain: *Ol dutar çalmagy öwrenmek isledi*: he wanted to learn to play the dutar.

questions.q: What does *sapak almaga* add in *halypasynyň öýüne sapak almaga barýar*?
options: why he goes: for a lesson
where he goes: to his master's house
questions.explain: `-mAgA` after *barmak* gives the purpose: to take a lesson.

questions.q: What is *çalyşyny* in *Halypasy onuň çalyşyny gowy görýär*?
questions.explain: *çalyş*, from *çalmak* with `-(Y)ş`: his playing, the way he plays.
